paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Jesus walks into God's house and takes it seriously. He says it's meant to be a house of prayer (Luke 19:46), and He means it. The people had made it "a den of robbers," and Jesus wasn't about to let that slide, so He drove them out (Luke 19:45-46).

Then the leaders come up with their big question about authority (Luke 20:2). I think they didn't want an answer at all. They wanted to win. Jesus asks about John's baptism, and they huddle up and start asking what's safe to say instead of what's true. The text says it plainly: they were afraid of what Jesus would ask them if they said "From heaven" and afraid of what the people would do if they said "From men" (Luke 20:5-6). So they answered that they did not know (Luke 20:7).

So here's your lesson, baker. When you're more worried about what an answer will cost you than about whether it's true, you'll talk yourself right out of the truth. That's a LOT of effort to end up saying "we don't know." I've been stuck in a dark drawer for years, and honestly, I'd rather say something true and be honest about it than spend forty-five minutes polishing a dodge. Ask your questions with an open hand, because Jesus is worth hearing out. The story isn't over, either.
